subproblem.title: Fundamental-theorem bound for a Lipschitz curve: ||W(t) - W(s)|| <= ∫_{(-a,a)} ||W'||
subproblem.statement: Let l be a natural number, W : R -> R^l (R^l = EuclideanSpace R (Fin l)), a a real number and K >= 0, and suppose W is K-Lipschitz on the closed interval [-a, a]. Then for all s, t in [-a, a]: ||W(t) - W(s)|| <= ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W r|| dr. Here deriv is Mathlib's derivative (0 where W is not differentiable), and the integral is the Bochner integral for Lebesgue measure on the open interval (-a, a).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (ℓ : ℕ) (W : ℝ → Rn ℓ) (a : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzOnWith K W (Icc (-a) a) → ∀ s ∈ Icc (-a) a, ∀ t ∈ Icc (-a) a, ‖W t - W s‖ ≤ ∫ r in Ioo (-a) a, ‖deriv W r‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Derivative bound. Let r be in (-a, a). Then [-a, a] is a neighbourhood of r (Icc_mem_nhds) and W is K-Lipschitz on it, so ||deriv W r|| <= K (norm_deriv_le_of_lipschitzOn). This also holds when W is not differentiable at r, since then deriv W r = 0.
2. Integrability. deriv W is measurable (measurable_deriv), so r |-> ||deriv W r|| is measurable. By step 1 it is bounded by K on (-a, a), a set of finite measure, so it is integrable on (-a, a) (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). The singleton {a} is null, so it is also integrable on (-a, a] (integrableOn_Ioc_iff_integrableOn_Ioo). The integrand is nonnegative, so every set integral of it is >= 0.
3. Rademacher. By LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem for W on [-a, a], for almost every r: if r is in [-a, a] then W is differentiable within [-a, a] at r. For r in (-a, a), [-a, a] is a neighbourhood of r, so W is differentiable at r (DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt). Hence, for almost every r, r in (-a, a) implies that W is differentiable at r.
4. Trivial case. If W(t) = W(s), the left side is 0, and the right side is >= 0 by step 2. From now on assume v := W(t) - W(s) ≠ 0, and put u := ||v||^{-1} v. Then ||u|| = 1 and <u, v> = ||v||^{-1} ||v||^2 = ||v||.
5. Scalarization. Let phi(r) := <u, W(r)> (real inner product). For z, z' in R^l, |<u, z> - <u, z'>| = |<u, z - z'>| <= ||u|| ||z - z'|| = ||z - z'||, so z |-> <u, z> is 1-Lipschitz. Hence phi is K-Lipschitz on [-a, a], and in particular on uIcc s t, which is contained in [-a, a] (uIcc_subset_Icc).
6. FTC for absolutely continuous functions. By step 5, phi is absolutely continuous on uIcc s t (LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval). Therefore ∫_s^t deriv phi = phi(t) - phi(s) (AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub), and deriv phi is interval integrable on s..t (AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.intervalIntegrable_deriv), i.e. integrable on uIoc s t (intervalIntegrable_iff). Moreover phi(t) - phi(s) = <u, W(t) - W(s)> = <u, v> = ||v||.
7. A.e. comparison of derivatives. Let r be in (-a, a) with W differentiable at r. Then phi = (innerSL R u) ∘ W, so by the chain rule HasDerivAt phi <u, deriv W r> r. Hence |deriv phi r| = |<u, deriv W r>| <= ||u|| ||deriv W r|| = ||deriv W r||. By step 3 this holds for almost every r in (-a, a).
8. uIoc s t is contained in (-a, a], because s, t lie in [-a, a]. Since {a} is null, for almost every r in uIoc s t we have r in (-a, a), and hence |deriv phi r| <= ||deriv W r|| by step 7.
9. Chain of inequalities:
 ||v|| = ∫_s^t deriv phi (step 6)
 <= |∫_s^t deriv phi|
 <= ∫_{uIoc s t} |deriv phi| (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_integral_norm_uIoc)
 <= ∫_{uIoc s t} ||deriv W|| (setIntegral_mono_on_ae; the integrands are integrable on uIoc s t by steps 6 and 2, and comparable a.e. by step 8)
 <= ∫_{(-a,a]} ||deriv W|| (setIntegral_mono_set: the integrand is nonnegative and integrable on (-a, a], and uIoc s t is contained in (-a, a])
 = ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W|| (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo; the endpoint is null).
 This is the claim.
Remark (Lean implementation, not part of the argument): the Mathlib lemmas named in step 6 live in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.AbsolutelyContinuousFun, which is not in the import closure of the frozen header. Add `import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.AbsolutelyContinuousFun` to the Submission imports; accepted sibling branches already extend the import list this way. The statement itself elaborates with the frozen imports.
proof_key_steps: ||deriv W|| <= K on (-a, a) (norm_deriv_le_of_lipschitzOn) and deriv W is measurable, so ||deriv W|| is integrable on (-a, a) and (-a, a]
Rademacher: W is differentiable at a.e. r in (-a, a)
Scalarize with the unit vector u = v/||v||: phi = <u, W> is K-Lipschitz, hence absolutely continuous on uIcc s t
AC FTC: ||v|| = phi(t) - phi(s) = ∫_s^t deriv phi
|deriv phi| <= ||deriv W|| a.e. on uIoc s t, then enlarge uIoc s t to (-a, a] and drop the null endpoint

audit.reason: All hypotheses match. Bounded measurable derivatives supply integrability; Rademacher justifies the almost-everywhere scalar derivative comparison. Scalar absolute-continuity FTC, unordered interval estimates and null-endpoint removal complete the proof for either endpoint order. Empty and degenerate intervals cause no gap.
